title: Wringer fleet manifest
description: `manifest.json` of a `wring fleet` bundle — the index of a supervised queue: what was declared, what the supervisor was configured to allow, and the honest terminal counts. `wringer.fleet.v1` moves independently of the evidence bundle, because a fleet REFERENCES the loops it drove (`loops`, by directory name) rather than containing them. Unlike the ledger beside it, this file is not scrubbed: it holds no command strings, only ids, counts and reasons.

fleet_id.description: The bundle directory's name — `YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-<4 hex>`, stamped in UTC so host and container runs of one repository sort together.

started_at.description: Local time with UTC offset, seconds precision. Local because a human reads it and the offset is the part they want; the id is the part that sorts.

config.description: The supervisor's declared bounds. Deliberately a SUBSET of the `fleet:` config section: these four decide what the supervisor did, and recording keys it merely parsed would imply they were exercised.

result.description: Honest partial success: three counts that sum to the declared task set, and whether the declared join condition held. A fleet that parked half its work reports it rather than rounding to failure.

tasks.description: Every declared task and how it ended. Terminal states only — a task still pending when the fleet stopped is parked, not omitted.

reason.description: Why it ended in that state. Empty for a task that simply succeeded — absence of a reason is itself the reason.

attempts.description: Spawns, not retries. 0 for a task parked before it ever ran — a missing directory, a worktree that could not be made, or a deadline that bit while it was queued.

loops.description: The loop bundle directory names this task produced, in order. References, not blobs: the loops carry their own evidence and their own chained ledgers.
